pallor morbum, vastatio regionis bellum:
quædam conjuncta sunt cum reiut[?] inæqualis
pulsatio arteriæ cum febri, tranquilitas
conscientiæ cum justificatione. Atque ex his
quædam dicuntur τεκμήρια[?], quædam
εἰκότα[?]. Τεκμήρια dicuntur, quæ omni & soli
rei signatæ conveniunt, atque adeò cum
illa reciprocantur; ut aurora cum Solis
ortu, fulmen cum tonitru: εἰκότα[?] dicun-
tur, quæ cum re signata non reciprocan-
tur, eaque vel omni conveniunt, non
soli; sic pallor est signum morbi; hæc
vocantur signa æquivoca: quædam con-
veniunt soli, non omni; sic eclipsis est
signum plenilunii: quædam nec omni, nec
soli; veluti cum cutis hispida, dicitur signum
falacitatis.
XIV. Circumstantia est id quod circa
rem est, sive adiacet aut appositum est;
huc pertinet locus, tempus, vestitus, armatura,
& id genus alia.
CAP. XXIX.

main_text.l: THESIS I.
Necessarium generatim dicitur, quod
non potest non esse: Necessario con-

page.notes: The Greek words τεκμήρια and εἰκότα are read from a small scan and marked [?]; their accents are uncertain. "reiut" (about "cum re ut") is uncertain, probably a printing error or a dropped letter. The second line of Thesis I continues on the next page with "trarium" (the word is "contrarium", split as "con-" / "trarium"); the printed hyphen is kept as "con-" only where it stands. The drop cap N in "Necessarium" is joined to the word. Lines of the thesis on the printed page: "Necessario con-" and "trarium" (the continuation "trarium" is at the right of the line below). No catchword, signature or notes in the margins.
